hints.content: In the sequence $~\dfrac{{2^{n}}}{n^2}~$, the exponential function in the numerator grows at a faster rate than the quadratic function in the denominator.  To see this, imagine letting $~n=1000\,$.  The numerator would have $~1000~$ factors of $~2~$, a huge number!  The denominator would have just 2 factors of 1000 (which is only about 10 factors of 2).

As $n\to \infty$, the numerator of the sequence grows much faster than the denominator.  

Hence,$\qquad\displaystyle\underset{n\to \infty }{\mathop{\lim }}\text{ }\frac{{{2}^{n}}}{n^2}=\infty\,$.
